Subject: Post-demo: Aurora POC finalists, bench links & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the clear goals you shared (multi-turn QA + policy enforcement, target 10–15k daily queries, strict hallucination constraints). Quick recap + our recommended shortlist and next steps so we have alignment before the pilot kick-off.

Recommended model finalists (tradeoff summary):
- LlamaX-13B (8-bit) — Rationale: strongest quality on our in-house QA set (F1-style accuracy ~0.78), best contextual handling for longer prompts; expected cost mid-tier; median token latency ~55–80ms on G5 class GPU with continuous batching. Good choice if accuracy is primary.
- Redwood-3-mini (quantized 4-bit) — Rationale: best cost/latency sweet spot for high throughput (token latency ~25–40ms), slightly lower answer fidelity on edge cases (F1 ~0.70) but excellent prefix-cache hit rates. Good if SLOs prioritize tail latency and unit cost.
- Mistral-7B (8-bit) — Rationale: lightweight quality uplift vs other 7B models with predictable latency (~30–45ms) and very low memory footprint; lower cost than 13B, better than some 7B baselines on hallucination tests. Good guardrail-friendly option.

Primary risks / considerations:
- Hallucination sensitivity on long multi-step prompts — we'll need prompt templates and L0 guardrails (verifier prompts / citation checks).
- Throughput spikes at peak hours — suggest a small dedicated pool + autoscale buffer.
- Metric alignment: propose we measure precision@1, hallucination rate (manual label sample), and latency p95 for acceptance.

Attachments / quick links: prompt pack + benchmark CSV attached. Full benchmark dashboard: https://drive.redwood/shared/aurora/prompt-pack-v2

Suggested next steps:
1) Approve shortlisted models for 48-hour pilot (we'll stage variants: 13B-8bit, Redwood-3-mini, Mistral-7B-8bit).
2) Redwood runs benchmark on your sample set and shared prompt pack (we'll provide a dropbox for results within 24h).
3) Plan a 2-week paid pilot on a small Dedicated pool (pricing below) — target kickoff: Mon Apr 2.

Commercial: high-level pilot cost estimate included in the attached note (we'll follow up with a formal quote once you confirm the scope).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call tomorrow if you want to walk the shortlist.

--

Elliot / team — quick tech notes to answer the hallucination + guardrail questions: 

- Hallucination numbers (rough samples from today's run on your prompts): LlamaX-13B ~ 28/100 hallucination flags (sampling + manual review), Redwood-3-mini ~ 34/100, Mistral-7B ~ 30/100. These are early numbers on ~300 sampled responses; we'll run a larger stratified sampling during the pilot.
- Why LlamaX looks better on QA: stronger context retention across chained prompts; its retrieval-integration pattern matched your doc snippets.
- Guardrails to run in-parallel during pilot: 1) deterministic verifier prompts (binary check); 2) extract-and-verify citations against your vector index (we can run an offboard checker); 3) conservative decoding for the most safety-sensitive intents (top-p tuning).
- Latency notes: with continuous KV cache and batching, expect p50 token latency in the ranges Vivek listed; p95 will depend on concurrency — we recommend a dedicated pool with a 20% burst capacity to keep p95 < 200ms.

I've attached the quick benchmark CSV (benchmarks_20280328.csv) showing token-level latencies across instance types and quant profiles. Also included the prompt templates in aurora_prompt_pack_v2.txt.

If you confirm the three models, I'll schedule the benchmark run for Friday and share the long-form report Monday.

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the questions — short answers and proposed commercial path below.

1) Hallucination rate: Marissa's sample numbers are representative; we'll run a 1k stratified sample during the pilot and report both absolute rates and severity buckets (minor/major). Acceptance criteria proposal: major hallucination rate < 5% on the 1k sample, precision@1 >= 0.72 for the primary QA intents.

2) Guardrails stack (pilot): runtime verifier (fast binary check), cite-extractor + index lookup, conservative decoding on top-of-stack for flagged intents. We'll deliver the verifier templates in the attached prompt pack.

3) Pilot pricing (2-week, Dedicated test pool with minimal burst): estimated $8,500 — covers Dedicated GPU hours for the three model variants, platform usage, and one SE-led bench/report. If you want a hands-on SRE-run, add $2,000. We'll convert to a formal quote once you confirm scope.

Commercial path / timeline:
- If you sign the pilot: kickoff Mon Apr 2; Marissa runs bench Friday; results Monday (Apr 1); pilot runs Apr 2–15; mid-pilot check-in Apr 9.
- Post-pilot: we'll present a decision brief and recommended production configuration (Dedicated vs Hosted + expected monthly cost).

Deal: AE-4892 (I've linked the HubSpot record here: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/AE-4892).

Next step: please confirm the three finalists for the pilot and whether to include the SRE add-on.
